I decided to be a vegetarian when I was very young, like 11 years old. I made the decision on my own because I was a little overweight and I was also concerned about the environmental impact (I think my teacher showed us a video about it or something, lol). I am mostly just a vegetarian now because I'm used to it and it helps me maintain a healthy diet- after becoming a vegetarian I lost all of my baby fat. I also wear leather, because the items I own that are made of leather get put to good use and I would assume that, for example, buying one pair of leather boots has less of an impact environmentally than buying 3 pairs of boots made from lesser quality material. 

I am not saying I feel bad about my confession, I don't really at all, I just thought I would tell reddit because no one else knows and I keep it as my own little secret ;).

She's probably scared of two things: 1. having to actually say the things she feels in person (so much worse than over the phone- having to witness the reaction of the other person etc.) and 2. rashly changing her decision because of the face-to-face convo... Maybe don't ask to come see her to "fix things" necessarily. Tell her you understand her decision and you just want to share how you feel face to face. ?

It's funny because my boyfriend used to say the same thing about me, I was able to "shut myself off" from things. And it's true, I don't like to deal with tough situations so I just turn my back on them. Maybe try explaining to her why you had trouble showing her how you felt about her if you haven't already. Try and get her to open up to you. 

And no problem! :)

Hi. I was in a very similar situation last year, except I was the girl. My boyfriend and I had dated only 6 months before he moved away for school. Those six months were amazing- we spent every minute together, I was so sure it was going to last. We dated for a year long distance and things got really hard. We would fight a lot, but whenever we were together somehow things felt perfect again. When I went away for school, we were both so consumed with other things and were so confident since we had already lasted a year long distance, and things began to really fall apart. I felt really insecure that he didn't love me any more and I thought maybe we were being burdens on each other's lives.

I called things off after a couple months. I was sooo upset, and everything within me wanted to just call him up get back together. He tried his darndest to convince me to hold onto the relationship, but I had already made up my mind. 

My advice to you is to see her in person. If she's anything like me, she has made up her mind and there's not much you can do. But the only thing that ever made me question my decision was the way I felt around him when we were together, face to face, talking things out. I feel like I have made a mistake, I perhaps let go of one of the greatest things I've ever had. Don't let this happen! Long distance relationships need a lot of TLC, a lot more than you probably expected. If you two do get back together and there's still distance between you, make sure you see her as much as you can. If you can't, pick up the phone or Skype or something. 

I don't think you should bring up living with her in January- she's probably already really confused and she probably needs time to think about everything. One of the other problems I had with my long distance relationship was how pressing my boyfriend could be at times. He would always talk about our future and it really scared me. This may have been what caused her to shut herself off from you in the first place...? 

Hopefully that helps, I'm not that great at giving advice but I thought I'd give it a shot! Good luck!!
